name: ExifTool
description: Perl library and CLI for reading, writing and editing metadata (EXIF, IPTC, XMP, GPS, maker notes) across a very wide range of image, video and audio formats.
journalism_use_case: First-pass verification of source-supplied media: extract capture time, GPS, camera make/model and software history to test whether a file's claimed origin is plausible.
data_licence_terms: No external data service; operates on local files only. Extracted metadata may contain personal data (home GPS, device serials) needing careful handling.
deployment: local CLI / Perl library; packaged in most distros, Homebrew, Windows binaries
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-10, 5266 stars, not archived. No GitHub Releases (versions shipped via exiftool.org).
external_deps: Perl runtime. No API keys, no network, no GPU.
data_flows: Entirely local: reads files on disk, writes report to stdout/file.
limitations: Metadata is trivially editable and is stripped by most social platforms, so absence proves nothing and presence proves only what the writer put there. Not a forgery detector.

name: Exiv2
description: C++ library and CLI to read and write image metadata including EXIF, IPTC, XMP and ICC profiles, used as the metadata engine inside many other applications.
journalism_use_case: Embed metadata extraction into a newsroom ingest pipeline so every incoming image is automatically parsed for timestamps and GPS before an analyst sees it.
data_licence_terms: No external data service; local file processing only.
deployment: system library plus CLI; bundled in digiKam, KDE and other tools
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-09, 1172 stars, not archived. LICENSE.txt states GPL version 2 or (at your option) any later version.
external_deps: C++ toolchain; optional zlib/expat. No API keys, no GPU.
limitations: Same fundamental caveat as all metadata tools: metadata is writer-controlled and routinely stripped, so it corroborates rather than proves. Engineer-facing, not an analyst UI.

name: ImageHash
description: Python library implementing average, perceptual, difference, wavelet, colour and crop-resistant image hashing, producing fingerprints stable under rescaling and recompression.
journalism_use_case: Cluster thousands of scraped images to find all re-uploads of one photo across accounts, or test whether an image circulating with a new caption is an old, already-located frame.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local images only.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-10-12, 3887 stars, not archived.
external_deps: Python, Pillow, NumPy/SciPy. No API keys, no GPU.
data_flows: Local only: images in, hash strings out.
limitations: Near-duplicate matching is a similarity signal, not identity proof; thresholds need tuning and yield false positives on visually similar distinct scenes and false negatives on heavy crops, mirroring and overlays. Does not detect manipulation.

name: ThreatExchange (PDQ / TMK+PDQF / vPDQ)
description: Meta's open-sourced content-matching toolkit: the PDQ photo hash, TMK+PDQF and vPDQ video hashes, reference implementations and the Hasher-Matcher-Actioner matching service.
journalism_use_case: Index known footage (e.g. frames from a verified incident video) and match at scale against newly collected social uploads to trace how a clip spreads and spot re-uploads with altered captions.
data_licence_terms: Software is BSD-3-Clause. The separate Meta ThreatExchange hash-sharing PLATFORM requires an approved partner account under its own terms; the open algorithms do not. No imagery bundled.
deployment: local libraries/CLIs; HMA deployable via Docker/AWS
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-09, 1411 stars, not archived. GitHub reported NOASSERTION; LICENSE file is a BSD licence for ThreatExchange software, Meta Platforms copyright.
external_deps: Per-language toolchains; container/cloud infra for HMA. No GPU for PDQ.
data_flows: Hashing is local. If connected to Meta's platform, hashes (not images) are exchanged under partner terms.
limitations: A hash match is a strong similarity signal, not proof of provenance or authenticity; video hashing degrades under re-encoding and editing. Designed for matching known content, not discovering manipulation.

name: imagededup
description: Python package for finding exact and near-duplicate images using multiple hashing methods plus CNN embeddings, with built-in evaluation of deduplication quality.
journalism_use_case: Deduplicate a large scraped image corpus before manual review, collapsing thousands of reposts into unique images so analyst time goes to genuinely new material.
data_licence_terms: No data service. CNN method downloads pretrained ImageNet weights with their own upstream terms.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2025-08-15, 5685 stars, not archived. Roughly 15 months without commits.
external_deps: Python; deep-learning runtime for the CNN method; GPU optional and only helpful for CNN embeddings.
data_flows: Local processing; model weights fetched once.
limitations: Duplicate groupings are similarity judgements requiring a tuned threshold; CNN embeddings cluster semantically similar but distinct images, which is wrong for forensic identity. Development has slowed.

name: pHash
description: The original perceptual hash C++ library computing robust fingerprints for images, audio and video, with DCT, radial and MH hash variants.
journalism_use_case: Match a short audio or video clip against a reference library to identify re-used broadcast or propaganda material, where image-only hashing is insufficient.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local media only.
deployment: build from source as a C++ library
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-06-09, 664 stars, not archived.
external_deps: C++ toolchain, CImg, FFmpeg for video/audio. No API keys, no GPU.
limitations: GPL-3.0 copyleft constrains embedding in closed newsroom products. Low-level library with sparse modern documentation; audio/video hashing needs careful parameterisation. Matches are similarity signals, not proof.

name: blockhash-python
description: Python implementation of the blockhash perceptual image hashing algorithm, which divides an image into blocks and derives a bit string from per-block median comparisons.
journalism_use_case: A simple, dependency-light hash for deduplicating image sets where a documented, interoperable algorithm matters more than peak accuracy.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local images only.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2023-10-31, 131 stars, not archived. Effectively dormant for about three years.
external_deps: Python, Pillow. No API keys, no GPU.
limitations: Dormant, small and superseded in practice by ImageHash and PDQ; blockhash is less robust than PDQ to cropping and overlays. Similarity signal only.

name: PySceneDetect
description: Python library and CLI detecting shot changes in video via content-aware, threshold, adaptive and histogram detectors, able to split video or export representative keyframes per scene.
journalism_use_case: Reduce long user-generated or CCTV footage to a manageable keyframe set for geolocation and reverse image search, and detect cuts revealing that a claimed single take is edited.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local video. Output frames inherit source footage rights.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-16, 5498 stars, not archived. Release v0.7.3 published 2026-11-08.
external_deps: Python, OpenCV; FFmpeg or mkvmerge for splitting. No API keys, no GPU.
limitations: Shot-boundary detection is heuristic and threshold-dependent: fades, camera shake and low light cause missed or spurious cuts. Detected cuts indicate editing but do not establish manipulation or intent.

name: Katna
description: Python library automating keyframe extraction from video and smart cropping of images, selecting frames by clustering on colour histograms plus blur and brightness filtering.
journalism_use_case: Automatically pick the most informative, least blurry frames from shaky phone footage to use as geolocation and reverse-image-search candidates.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local media only.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2024-08-06, 401 stars, not archived. About two years without commits.
external_deps: Python, OpenCV, FFmpeg. No API keys, no GPU.
limitations: Frame selection is optimised for visual appeal and diversity, not evidential completeness, so it can discard the one frame that matters; always verify against the full video. Maintenance has stalled and dependency pinning is dated.

name: Sherloq
description: Open-source desktop image-forensics suite with a GUI bundling metadata and structure inspection, JPEG quality/ghost and quantisation analysis, error level analysis, noise and PRNU estimation, clone detection and enhancement filters.
journalism_use_case: Run a structured battery of forensic checks on a suspicious photograph to generate leads about splicing, resaving or local editing before escalating to a specialist lab.
data_licence_terms: No external data service; all analysis local on user-supplied images.
language_stack: Python with Qt GUI and OpenCV (GitHub linguist reports Perl, apparently a detection artefact)
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-07-16, 3263 stars, not archived.
external_deps: Python, PySide/Qt, OpenCV, ExifTool. No API keys, no GPU.
data_flows: Entirely local; evidence images are not uploaded to third parties.
limitations: Every output is a probabilistic signal, never conclusive proof of manipulation. Error level analysis and similar techniques are widely misread: social-media recompression, screenshots and filters all create artefacts that mimic tampering. Requires expert interpretation and must not be presented as a verdict.

name: c2pa-rs / c2patool
description: Rust implementation of the C2PA content-provenance specification with the c2patool CLI for reading, validating and attaching cryptographically signed Content Credentials describing capture and edit history.
journalism_use_case: Validate Content Credentials on images from C2PA-enabled cameras and tools to confirm a signed capture-and-edit chain, and sign the newsroom's own published assets for downstream verification.
data_licence_terms: No data service. Full trust validation depends on certificate trust lists; production signing requires certificates that may carry CA costs.
language_stack: Rust with bindings for other languages
deployment: local library / CLI; embeddable in services
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-16, 448 stars, not archived. Repo root contains both LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT.
external_deps: Rust toolchain; certificates and trust list for signing/validation. No GPU.
data_flows: Local validation of embedded manifests; optional network fetch for trust-list checks.
limitations: Only informative for files that carry credentials, and absence of a manifest is extremely common and means nothing. A valid signature proves who signed and the declared history, not that the depicted scene is real; stripping credentials is trivial. Adoption remains partial.

name: VFRAME
description: Computer-vision toolkit built for human-rights research on large video and image archives, with pipelines for object detection (including custom munitions detectors), frame extraction, redaction and metadata handling.
journalism_use_case: Triage very large conflict-footage archives by flagging frames likely to contain a specific object, such as a cluster-munition remnant, so investigators review a shortlist instead of thousands of hours.
data_licence_terms: No bundled data service. Custom detector models and training datasets are distributed separately with their own terms; source footage rights stay with the archive owner.
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2023-05-28, 76 stars, not archived. Dormant for roughly three and a half years.
external_deps: Python, OpenCV, deep-learning runtime; NVIDIA GPU strongly recommended. No paid API.
limitations: Detector outputs are probabilistic signals requiring human confirmation of every hit, never conclusive identification. Long dormancy means dependency rot is likely. Custom models are domain-specific and degrade on unfamiliar footage.

name: Bellingcat smart-image-sorter
description: User-friendly zero-shot image classification tool using open models from the Hugging Face library to sort image collections by user-supplied labels without training.
journalism_use_case: Triage a large unsorted image dump by describing the categories you care about in plain words (for example 'military vehicle', 'street protest', 'document scan') and letting the model bucket images for review.
data_licence_terms: Tool is Apache-2.0. Downloads third-party model WEIGHTS from Hugging Face whose individual licences vary (some are non-commercial or gated) and must be checked per model before newsroom use.
deployment: local CLI or notebook; GPU optional
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2024-08-14, 68 stars, not archived. About 15 months without commits.
external_deps: Python, transformers; model weight downloads (GB-scale); GPU helpful not required. No paid API.
data_flows: Local inference after weights download; images are not uploaded if run locally.
limitations: Zero-shot classification is an unreliable triage aid, not a labelling authority: accuracy varies sharply with label wording and it fails on fine-grained military or technical distinctions. Every bucket needs human review, and counts derived from it must not be published unvalidated.
